name: Quantitative statistics and reporting rules (package 1): R0-R2 and test family F1
registered: 2026-10-21, before any new evaluation run of package 1
status: Every test split covered here (Replica, ScanNet and NeRF-Object-Removal test) had ALREADY been evaluated and read when this file was written (quant_review.md, section 1h). F1 is therefore a declared family over results already seen: its tests are descriptive and post hoc. No primary test is declared. scripts/quant_stats.py reads the family from this file and refuses a family that differs from it.

rules.R0: Report everything. Every analysis that runs is reported, in the main text or the appendix, whatever its outcome.
R1: The unit is the scene. Use one paired test everywhere: the exact two-sided sign test, ties dropped.
Wilcoxon appears only as a complete secondary column, never picked per cell.
The effect size is the median paired difference in the metric's own unit. Relative gains appear only as medians.
No "primary" test is declared on results already seen.

"Significant" means Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 within a declared family: F1: the 20 tests of 1a. F2: ours+depth vs each of the 4 new fused rows, at G-AP and P-AP (8 tests). F3: package-2 claims, each declared in its own prereg before it runs.
rules.R2: Aggregation. Show the per-scene mean and the pixel-pooled value side by side. Claim a calibration difference only if it holds under both and in x/N.

F1.text: the 20 tests of 1a: ours vs each of 4 baselines on 5 Table I metrics, paired over the 14 test scenes (Replica 6 + ScanNet 8)
F1.label: post hoc summary over results already seen; the per-dataset x/N is the main description, the pooled 14-scene test mixes a synthetic and a real dataset

records.replica: uags_results/tab1/eval_test.json (identical to docs/reports/2026-09-29-replica-tab1/logs/eval_test_224fe1e.json, the source of Table I)

F1.values: metrics.scenes[s].rows[r].all[metric] (variant all: the coverage rule, uncovered pixels count as wrong)
F1.ours_rows_text: mIoU uses ours_P0 (P0 and P2 share labels). The other columns use ours_P2.

legs.rule: lambda_u chosen on validation (scripts/make_tables.py choose --key legs)

F1.difference: per scene, signed so that positive = ours better: (baseline - ours) for lower-is-better metrics, (ours - baseline) for mIoU
F1.test: exact two-sided sign test over the 14 pooled scenes, ties (difference exactly 0) dropped
F1.effect_size: median paired difference over the 14 scenes, in the metric's own unit; per-dataset medians and x/N also printed
F1.secondary: Wilcoxon signed-rank p (scipy.stats.wilcoxon, zeros dropped) for all 20 tests, as a complete column

F2.text: ours+depth vs each of the 4 new fused rows, at G-AP and P-AP (8 tests)
F2.status: not run by this package (needs the GPU dump of package 1, step 2-3)

F3.text: package-2 claims, each declared in its own prereg before it runs

aggregation.calibration: ECE as the mean over scenes AND pooled over pixels from the stored 15-bin reliability bins (metrics.scenes[s].rows[r].all.reliability: count, conf, acc); NLL and Brier as the scene mean AND pixel-weighted (n_pixels); both are always shown side by side
aggregation.check: each scene's ECE recomputed from its bins must equal the stored ECE (scripts/quant_stats.py seg stops otherwise)
aggregation.claim_rule: a calibration difference is written only if it has the same sign under both aggregations and ours is better in more than half of the scenes of that dataset (x/N)

descriptive: Every other p-value printed by scripts/quant_stats.py (per-dataset sign tests, P0 in place of P2, averaging vs the trained baselines, NOR paired comparisons, views comparisons) is descriptive: unadjusted, never called significant, always shown with x/N.
